stem_text: A body at rest is moved along a horizontal straight line by a machine delivering a constant power. The distance moved by the body in time 't' is proportional to :

candidate_solve.derivation: By Work-Energy Theorem: Total work done W = P * t. Assuming initial rest: 1/2 m v^2 = P * t => v^2 proportional to t => v proportional to t^(1/2). Distance x = integral v dt proportional to integral t^(1/2) dt proportional to t^(3/2). Matches Option A.
candidate_solve.limiting_cases: If constant force F acted, v proportional to t and x proportional to t^2. Under constant power P, force F = P/v decreases as speed increases, so distance grows as t^(3/2) (between linear and quadratic).

concept_model_selection.evidence: Work-energy theorem for constant power engine Pt = (1/2)mv^2

representation_translation.evidence: Scaling analysis v proportional to t^(1/2)

reasoning_chain_length.evidence: Integrating proportional speed to find distance proportional to t^(3/2)

trap_exception_sensitivity.evidence: Separating distance proportional to t^(3/2) from linear or quadratic rates

difficulty_evidence.differences: Rescored to native five-factor rubric per B2 CP-4 review

demand_proposal.rationale: Applying work-energy scaling to find power of time t
